memory_candidates.content: When a plan's Scope Hypothesis flags an axiom-profile measurement as uncertain and pre-writes a two-branch mitigation (one branch if the measured profile matches an existing claim, another if it does not), the non-matching branch is not a failure or a deviation -- it is a planned outcome with its own pre-written instructions. Execute the named branch exactly: never widen an existing multi-declaration axiom-profile claim (e.g. "all N report [propext] only") to cover a new name whose measured profile differs; instead add the new name's measured profile on its own line/paragraph with one sentence naming the specific step that costs the extra axiom (traceable to a specific lemma's own proof technique, e.g. a classical by_contra discharge), and add an explicit scoping sentence to any prose claim that would otherwise read as covering the new name.
